title: Resolve interleaved SSE delimiters and token-boundary loss in streaming API
author: Asha Patel
description: This change addresses a class of streaming failures where partial JSON tokens emitted across SSE chunks could be mis-parsed when delimiter bytes (newlines / `data:` markers) were interleaved with token bytes. Root cause: the old parser treated SSE delimiters and JSON byte sequences as independent, which allowed reassembly to drop or reorder delimiter context when incoming TCP/HTTP chunk boundaries split tokens atypically (common with proxies and multiplexed HTTP/2 connections). The fix implements a small lookahead buffer and an explicit synthetic-frame sentinel that is emitted by the stream adapter whenever we detect an incomplete JSON token at a chunk boundary. The parser FSM was updated to (1) prefer consuming delimiter markers only when they are not currently in the middle of a buffered JSON token, (2) treat the synthetic sentinel as an unconditional commit point for any buffered token, and (3) map OpenAI-style terminal sequences (e.g. "data: [DONE]") into the same terminal event flow used internally so tool/function-calling boundaries remain consistent. Also added a set of targeted fuzz tests and an e2e fixture that runs the OpenAI-compat adapter behind a proxy that induces random chunk splits. Backwards-compatible: the streaming wire protocol has not changed; the synthetic sentinel is internal-only. This PR includes docs clarifying streaming error codes and guidance for SDK authors on validating token boundaries. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for 48 hours in canary, then promoted to main if no regressions are observed. See validation_steps for test commands and expected outputs.
commits: parser: introduce lookahead buffer to preserve delimiter context
sse: emit explicit synthetic boundary when transitioning incomplete JSON tokens
compat: map OpenAI 'data: [DONE]' sequences to internal terminal events
tests: add fuzz tests for fragmented JSON and interleaved newline cases
docs: clarify streaming guarantees and add SDK validation snippet
diff_snippets:
// lookahead buffer: hold bytes across chunk boundaries until committed
var lookahead []byte

// synthetic sentinel used only internally to denote commit point
const sseSyntheticCommit = '\u0000'

// in stream_adapter: map OpenAI 'data: [DONE]' -> internal.TerminalEvent()
if line == "data: [DONE]" { emitTerminal() }
review_comments: Liam Chen: The FSM change makes sense, but can we avoid an extra allocation on the hot path? Suggest reusing a pooled buffer for lookahead.

Nina Roberts: Please add a regression test that reproduces the proxy-chunking symptom we saw in the incident log. Also add a short note to the streaming docs about the error code that indicates a malformed partial token.
Carlos Méndez: Were there any latency regressions in the bench? Even small allocations can amplify at 1k+tps; please include before/after p95 numbers.
author_responses: Asha Patel: Reworked lookahead to use sync.Pool-backed buffer; added unit that simulates 1k tps with pooled buffers; p95 is unchanged within noise.
Asha Patel: Added a deterministic proxy fixture in pkg/testing and a reproduction test that mirrors the incident. Document updated with streaming error guidance.
Asha Patel: Bench results included in the PR comment thread: p50 unchanged, p95 +1.8ms on microbenchmark (within acceptable SLO); e2e p95 unchanged.
release_notes: Fix: Streaming API now correctly handles interleaved delimiters and partial JSON tokens split across chunk boundaries. Impact: reduces rare malformed-output and tool-calling failures when proxies or HTTP/2 cause atypical chunking. Migration: none required for API consumers; SDKs updated to include validation helpers.
validation_steps: Run fuzz suite: go test ./pkg/testing -run TestSSEFuzz -fuzz=Fragmentation
Simulate proxy chunking: ./scripts/proxy-chunk-sim --split-pattern=random --target http://localhost:8080/stream and ensure that JSON objects reassemble without loss
SDK smoke: python -m examples.streaming.validate_token_boundaries --endpoint http://localhost:8080/stream (expect: 0 malformed-token errors)
